sections.h2: How quickly can a Monroe house sell?
sections.html:
Cash buyers who take the house as is tend to close ahead of a listing, because there is no lender to wait on and no repair list to negotiate. A well-kept house may still net more on the open market if your calendar is flexible.

Monroe suits both routes. The city sits inside Union County, where the assessor reported a median home value of $403,000 after a 2025 reappraisal. Before accepting an offer, ask each buyer about their closing date, the closing costs they cover and whether the price moves after inspection.

  • Listing: fits a clean house and a seller who can wait.
  • Cash buyer: the better fit when repairs, a tenant or a deadline make tours impractical.
  • Either way, hold two written offers before signing.

Monroe had an estimated 42,644 residents on July 1, 2025, up 23.1% from the 34,637 base in 2020. The 2010 count was 32,797. The city covers 30.61 square miles of land.

About 61.6% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-held home is valued at $309,100. Median gross rent is $1,246 and median household income is $72,540, with 2.86 people per household and a 30.1 minute average commute.

That $309,100 median is lower than the county assessor's 2025 median of $403,000, because the two figures cover different homes, years and areas. Do not assume either one is your price. The sizable rental share means landlords are active buyers, so a rented house can find a buyer who wants the income.

Monroe is updating its Downtown Master Plan, with a consulting firm hired by City Council to lead the work. The plan covers development, investment, mobility, public spaces and housing, and it expands the 2008 planning area to include more sub-districts.

The work runs in three phases, with the draft and final plan, an implementation roadmap and adoption by the Downtown Advisory Board and City Council scheduled through winter 2027. The study identified seven potential opportunity redevelopment sites. If your house is close to downtown, read the plan documents on the city's site, since a buyer may ask whether the plan touches your street. Dickerson Park, Lake Twitty and the downtown events are worth mentioning if your house is near them.

Monroe operates its own utilities, including a natural gas division. Keep recent utility bills ready, because buyers ask about monthly costs.

  • Ask the city before you cap or move a gas line.
  • Check the city's drought page for the watering stage in force before you stage the yard.

sections.h2: Trash pickup and clearing a house
sections.html:
The city contracts with Waste Pro. Households get weekly garbage, bulk and yard waste service, and recycling every other week, using a green 96-gallon garbage cart and a black 96-gallon recycling cart. Carts can go out from 5 p.m. the evening before, must sit within four feet of the street by 7 a.m., and must come in by 7 p.m. on pickup day to avoid a violation.

Garbage must be bagged, and grass clippings, electronics, construction debris and hazardous waste do not belong in the cart. Call Solid Waste at 704-282-4565 about missed pickups, bulky items or the back door collection offered to qualifying residents. Those rules are handy while you empty a house before listing it.

The city's Permit Center handles applications through its CityView portal, where a plan set must be uploaded as flattened PDF files. Inspection requests have a cut-off of 3 p.m. on the business day before the visit, and the center's phone line is 704-282-4524.

If you have open permits from a past renovation, get them closed before you list. A buyer's attorney can ask about them, and an open permit can slow a closing.

sections.h2: Union County property tax in Monroe
sections.html:
Union County mails the bill. The county rate in its 2026-2027 notice is 43.42 cents per $100 of assessed value, and owners who do not escrow receive four payment vouchers.

Union County tax bill timing
DateWhat applies
September 1Bill is due
January 5, 2027Last day to pay without interest on the 2026 bill

A general reappraisal took place in 2025, with notices of new values in March of that year. Since then, new notices go out only where a property changed through new construction, an addition, demolition or renovation. Ask Tax Administration how city tax shows up for your parcel.

To pay in person, go to the Tax Collector's Office on the first floor of the Union County Government Center, 500 N. Main St., Suite 119. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Recording the Monroe deed and what it costs
sections.html:
Your deed is filed with the Union County Register of Deeds. The office has served the county since 1842 and is a recording office only, so it will not draft papers or interpret them. A closing attorney prepares your deed.

The state sets recording charges: $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. On top of that, the seller pays a $1.00 excise tax per $500 of value before recording.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A Monroe sale goes faster when the paperwork is ready. Find your deed, your most recent Union County tax bill and a payoff letter from your lender. If the house is rented, add the lease, the rent ledger and the deposit record. If you renovated, gather permits and invoices, and confirm that each permit is closed.

Ask every buyer for a written offer that shows the price, the closing date, who pays which closing cost and what happens if inspection turns up a problem. A closing attorney then searches title, prepares the deed and the settlement statement, and files the deed with the Register of Deeds. Review the statement line by line before you sign. The loan payoff, any tax owed and the excise tax come out of your proceeds, and you receive the rest.

With a cash buyer, the schedule depends mostly on the title search, so you can often pick a closing date that fits your move. With a listing, plan for showings, an inspection and the buyer's loan approval before you can count on a closing day.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house in Monroe
sections.html:
North Carolina ties a landlord's notice to the kind of tenancy. A month-to-month tenant gets seven days, a week-to-week tenant two days, and a year-to-year tenancy needs a month or more of warning. Disputes go to a magistrate in small claims court. If a cash buyer is interested, ask whether they would keep your tenant.

Before you talk to buyers, pull together the lease, the rent ledger and the deposit record. An investor keeping the tenant will want to see the income documented.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Monroe house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers purchase as is. A listing, on the other hand, usually brings repair requests after the buyer's inspection, and any open permits should be closed with the city's Permit Center before you list.

faqs.q: Which office handles my property tax bill?
faqs.a: Union County Tax Administration. The bill is due September 1, and payments after January 5, 2027 draw interest on the 2026 bill. Ask the office how city tax appears on your parcel.

faqs.q: When did Union County last reappraise property?
faqs.a: In 2025, with value notices mailed that March. Since then the county sends new notices only where a property changed.

faqs.q: When do Monroe's recycling carts go out?
faqs.a: Recycling is collected every other week. The city's Solid Waste office, at 704-282-4565, can confirm which week your street is on.

faqs.q: Is the median of $309,100 my home's value?
faqs.a: No. That is a city-wide figure. Condition, size, location and your offers set the price.
